source: NASA PDS / Science (Hassler et al. 2014) / Science in the Classroom

gcrBaseline.measurementPeriod: First 300 Sols of MSL Mission (August 7, 2012 to June 1, 2013 / Sols 13 to 300)

provenance.methodology: Silicon semiconductor detector stacks (A, B, C) and plastic/CsI scintillators (D, E, F) measuring charged particle dE/dx and neutral particle fluxes.
provenance.limitations: Surface measurement in Gale Crater at -4.5 km depth; Martian atmospheric column (~20 g/cm^2) attenuates ~30% of GCR flux compared to high-altitude plateaus.

sol242SepEvent.measurementClarification: The reported +0.05 mSv (50 uSv) represents the integrated excess dose equivalent above background accumulated over the Sol 242 event pass (~50 uGy with quality factor <Q> ~ 1 for solar energetic protons), NOT a continuous daily rate. Peak surface absorbed dose rate reached ~260 uGy/day (a transient rate enhancement of ~50 uGy/day above the ~210 uGy/day baseline).

provenance.methodology: Direct detection of solar energetic protons and secondary atmospheric showers by RAD detector telescope.
provenance.limitations: Hard solar particle event during solar conjunction. Note: NASA DONKI WSA-ENLIL simulations for CME 2013-04-11T07:36:00-CME-001 modeled Spitzer/Earth shock arrivals, not a confirmed Mars shock arrival; therefore, we document the surface detection empirically without asserting an unverified DONKI shock-arrival model link.
